message.content:
As of my latest update (mid‑2026), **“Avatar”** remains the highest‑grossing film worldwide when measured at nominal box office receipts—over $2.9 billion since its original 2009 release.  

If you adjust for ticket price inflation or consider domestic-only grosses, other titles climb:

| Rank | Film | Nominal Worldwide Gross* | Inflation‑Adjusted Domestic Gross |
|------|------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1    | *Avatar* (2010) | ≈$2.92 B | — |
| 2    | *Avengers: Endgame* (2019) | ≈$2.79 B | ≈$7–8 B (inflation‑adjusted) |
| 3    | *Titanic* (1997) | ≈$2.19 B | ≈$10+ B |

\*Nominal figures reflect total theatrical revenue without accounting for currency fluctuations or re‑releases beyond the initial run.

So while “Avatar” tops the list in raw dollars earned from theaters, if you're looking at how many tickets were sold relative to today's prices—or comparing only U.S./Canada earnings—the picture changes slightly.
